Independent enumeration by sequential forcing and symmetric-difference adjacency
correctness.rationale: If three whites are in one part, no opposing vertex can make the first force into that part. A white pair in a part needs a special index, and for two white pairs an initial force exists exactly when the special-index signatures differ. For each of the resulting types the explicit two forces leave a singleton in each part, and there are at least two opposite blue vertices for each singleton, so they can both be forced. Thus the minimum sets leave four whites. A token jump on their complements fixes one pair and changes one member of the other. Within a family this means a rook move; across families the fixed pair must be {1,2} and the changed pair must retain its nonspecial member, yielding exactly the identical-boundary bridges. They restore lost puncture degrees. The punctured rook diameter is at most two and every vertex is within one step of a bridge. Interior points across copies with no shared coordinate have no common bridge label and need four steps; with one nonspecial row or column, all interior points share a bridge label and the cross-copy distances are at most three. Opposite interiors give distance at least three. The vertex and edge formulas follow directly. Independent enumeration of four-white forcing closures and every labelled adjacency confirmed the exact claimed structure and the diameter in all 36 cases 3≤a,b≤8 (1,386 vertices and 5,796 edges total).
residual_risks: The finite check is corroboration; the proof, not the finite range, handles all part sizes.

Resultary dbea30a31d6d for the distinction between counting and reconfiguring
value.rationale: The graph structure identifies how a natural perturbation of a biclique changes the entire minimum-set exchange geometry, not just the support count. The identity bridges provide an explicit adjacency model and explain exactly why small part size changes the maximum reconfiguration distance. This is a uniform result on two unrestricted part sizes, including both boundary regimes.
residual_risks: Does not address arbitrary matching deletions, token sliding or nonminimum sets.
